title: Audience Favor
summary: Currency earned from Twitch Drop Festivals, achievement rewards, or Brother Pela’s Time Crystal exchange.
sections: Redeem a Drop Festival reward

Claim Drop awards 1 Audience Favor. The player-reported price is 400 Twitch Channel Points. Open Streams in Microscape and choose a live Twitch channel marked at Drop Festival or Drop & Dungeon. Check the Claim Drop tile in the Channel Points menu below Twitch chat before redeeming. In Microscape, check Journal → History → Audience Favors for the channel name and +1.
Get a head start on Channel Points

Twitch awards 300 points the first time you follow a channel with Channel Points enabled. If your balance was zero, you’ll need 100 more points for a 400-point Claim Drop. Earn them in the channel hosting the festival.
Earn Favor without Channel Points

In the Tome of Knowledge → Achievements, Equip your first weapon or tool to earn 3 Favor from your first-weapon achievement. The Journey Begins instead awards a Bazaar Invite at level 10 in any skill, and Awakening Power awards 6 for your first ability limit break. At Falcrest Reach Temple, Brother Pela trades 1 Time Crystal for 1 Favor at Piety 1.
Favor and Energy in Streams

Use Streams to find live Microscape Twitch communities. Their Channel Points menu may also offer Energy rewards, such as +6hr for Me. A 1.2× or 1.3× badge means 72 or 78 minutes of in-game Energy per eligible hour watched, respectively. It doesn’t affect your Favor or Twitch Channel Points.
Pet-map prices at release

Mork’s new skilling-pet maps cost 10 Audience Favor; his original skilling-pet maps cost 20. Beatrix and Scales maps remain 10. Otis’s maps cost 15 and require Adventurer’s Guild membership to obtain the pet. Check the individual pet page for eligible tasks and current odds.

title: Double Up Bonus
summary: Each effective skill level above an activity’s required level adds one percentage point of double-up chance, capped at 100%.
sections: Chance calculation

For an XP-awarding skilling action, the client calculates: chance (%) = min(100, max(0, effective skill level − activity required level)). Effective skill level includes your base level, temporary stat boosts and the relevant equipped skill bonuses.
Worked example

A level-30 miner with +3 Mining equipment doing a level-15 activity has an effective level of 33 and an 18% double-up chance. A level-15 miner with no bonus on the same activity has 0%. The chance cannot exceed 100%.
What a double-up does

A successful double-up quickly repeats the eligible action. The October 21 rules count it as a regular action, so account for the repeated action’s materials and outputs. Abilities such as Iron Gut, Sweet Tooth and Sour Stomach can interact with double-ups. Actions with no positive base XP show no ordinary double-up chance in the checked client.

title: Level
summary: Skill levels come from XP; player combat level combines base offensive levels with Defense.
sections: Skill levels and experience

Each skill has its own XP total. The client derives a base level from that total using the shared XP curve. Skill pages list level-gated activities and equipment, and the XP calculator can estimate progress between levels. Ability levels and permanent unlocks are separate from a player’s combat level.
Player combat-level formula

Combat level = floor((max((Attack + Strength) / 2, Evil Magic, Ranged) + Defense) / 2). Use base skill levels. Temporary boosts and equipment bonuses are not added by this formula. The strongest offensive route is combined with Defense; raising an unused weaker offensive route may not immediately increase combat level.
Foe combat levels

Foes use a separate formula: max(1, floor((((Attack + Strength) / 2) + Defense) / 2)). Their HP, Evil Magic and Ranged stats are still relevant in combat but are not inputs to this displayed foe-level calculation.

title: Ticks
summary: The standard game tick is 2 seconds; activity definitions and attack delays are expressed in ticks.
sections: Reading activity times

The client displays standard skilling time as (action duration + 4 preparation ticks) × 2 seconds. For example, a five-tick action is 10 seconds of action plus 8 seconds of preparation, or 18 seconds in the activity details.
What the estimate includes

Preparation is not the same as the action itself. Travel, banking, combat interruptions and special activity behavior can add time. A page labelled action duration excludes preparation; a base-time column includes it unless stated otherwise.
Combat and bonus actions

A foe’s base delay is also stored in ticks. Boss phases and multi-hit behavior can produce a different visible pattern. Double-up actions repeat quickly and should not be timed as a second full preparation cycle.

title: Vendor
summary: An item’s vendor value is its base sell price; shop purchase prices use that shop’s markup.
sections: Selling to a shop

For items with a numeric sell value, the shop UI uses the item’s base value as its sell price. Do not assume an item with no listed sell value can be sold. Inventory and loot-bag management are separate from creating a player-to-player Bazaar offer.
Buying from a shop

Purchase price = floor(item base value × shop multiplier). A shop-specific multiplier for an item overrides the shop’s general multiplier. For example, the General Store uses a 3× markup, while Merric’s Magic Shop applies a special 14× markup to Staff.
Choosing between shops and the Bazaar

Shop stock is a fixed list. The Bazaar is player trading, so its offers can differ from vendor value. The client warns when an order is at or below vendor value and may hide it from the normal listing; use the current in-game price and fees when comparing options.

sections: How to get there
New characters begin at Tutabay Atoll. From Fencewell Bridge, use the boat's Sail to Tutabay Atoll activity to return to the island.
Leaving for Progryn

Thomas exchanges one Rodent Pelt or one Bronze Dagger for a Ticket to Progryn. Hand the ticket to the island boat to sail to Fencewell Bridge. The client also defines a one-time abandoned-hut search that yields a ticket; that activity is hidden from the normal map/activity lists.
Starting supplies

Jaciens' Supplies sells a Training Pickaxe for 7 coins and a Training Fishing Rod for 4 coins. Lucille exchanges one Copper Ore for one Tin Ore. Island Rodents drop Bones and have a 1 in 2 chance of dropping a Rodent Pelt.
